RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is not evidence of anything. Panels reflect who holds senior roles in a field; laboratory medicine and hospital administration are heavily female-staffed, so four women is unremarkable. Raising it would signal that you read a hiring loss as conspiracy, which damages you far more than it helps — including with future applications in the same organisation.

Your real grievance is procedural: you requested a written explanation and got silence. That is concrete, documentable and often legally required. Chase it in writing, cite the relevant statute or policy, and set a deadline.

If the explanation, once received, shows the criteria were rewritten to fit her profile, you have something. Credentials alone don't decide appointments — leadership hires often favour management experience over research depth.
